findings.headline: Stress spike on lap 19 coincides with wet track and DRS loss but did not degrade position
findings.detail: Stress spiked to 62 on lap 19 as the track went wet and DRS was disabled; despite a 7.3s pace delta the driver held P2 with a 0.2s gap, indicating the stress was reactionary rather than performance‑limiting. No further stress spikes occurred after the tyre change to Intermediates, so the driver coped well once the wet tyre was fitted.
evidence: DRS disabled race control -8s on lap 19

findings.headline: Medium tyres degraded slowly; lap 15 pace gain suggests driver lifted to manage cooling track
findings.detail: The medium tyre stint (laps 1‑27) showed a modelled degradation of +0.147 s/lap while pace stayed within ±0.2 s until lap 15, after which a sudden -0.526 s improvement occurred (lap 15) likely due to the driver lifting to preserve grip as the track cooled to 24.6 °C.
evidence: modelled deg +0.147 s/lap for medium stint

findings.headline: Intermediates gave a performance boost on wet track (negative degradation)
findings.detail: After switching to Intermediates on lap 28, the modelled degradation turned negative (-0.116 s/lap) and pace improved by up to -0.596 s (lap 30) despite the track remaining wet, indicating the intermediate tyres provided a clear performance advantage on the wet surface.
evidence: modelled deg -0.116 s/lap for intermediate stint

findings.headline: Softs held pace despite slight degradation; rain on lap 45 caused a minor slowdown
findings.detail: During the soft tyre stint (laps 40‑52) the modelled degradation was +0.123 s/lap, yet pace remained within ±0.27 s; the only notable slowdown was on lap 45 (+0.122 s) when rain returned, suggesting the softs were marginally sensitive to brief wet patches.
evidence: modelled deg +0.123 s/lap for soft stint

findings.headline: Blue‑flag traffic caused a +1.25 s pace loss on lap 26
findings.detail: Blue flags appeared from lap 21 onward while the driver was on medium tyres; the only lap with a measurable pace delta during blue‑flag periods was lap 26 (+1.249 s), likely reflecting traffic management rather than tyre performance.

findings.headline: Driver remains calm until wet conditions arrive, stress only spikes at lap 19
findings.detail: Radio calls at laps 4 and 11 show calm stress (≈43) despite the driver noting a potential shower; the lack of stress rise before the actual wet onset suggests the driver’s anticipation does not translate into measurable stress until conditions change.
